summary: Target-level plan for the cyclotomic main conjectures of modular forms. L0 fixes the modular Iwasawa datum (geometric normalisation, the Skinner–Urban twist T = T_f(det ρ_f^{-1}), Λ = O[[Γ]] and Λ(G_∞)), constructs the ordinary Selmer dual, the ordinary p-adic L-function with canonical periods, Kato's Iwasawa cohomology and fundamental line and the LLZ signed Selmer groups, states the three main conjectures as propositions, and proves the structure theorem and the two comparisons (Kato 17.13; LLZ Corollary 6.6). L1 proves the Skinner–Urban form (requested by HE.0 and BSD.0), the Fouquet–Wan 1.6 form along FW §4.8, the Selmer form and Skinner's multiplicative-reduction theorem; L2–L4 import Fouquet–Wan's pointwise and family endpoints and the BCS theorems from AutomorphicCongruences (RS-11 narrowings) and prove the convention, lattice/period and signed comparisons; L5 gives Euler-factor, coefficient and μ/λ invariance, the rank-zero converse, the ℒ-invariant, the Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum conjecture, trivial zeros, Schneider's implication and verified examples (11a1 at 7, 14a1 at 13 and 5, η⁴(z)η⁴(5z) at 7); L6 is the interface to the separately proved anticyclotomic, Eisenstein, supersingular and multiplicative branches.

nodes.title: The modular Iwasawa datum
nodes.statement: A modular Iwasawa datum D = (f, p, L, T_f) consists of: an odd prime p with fixed embeddings ι_∞ : Q̄ → C and ι_p : Q̄ → Q̄_p; a newform f ∈ S_k(Γ_1(N), ε) of weight k ≥ 2; a finite extension L/Q_p containing ι_p(Q(f)), with ring of integers O, uniformiser ϖ and residue field F; the two-dimensional L-representation ρ_f : G_Q → Aut_L(V_f) of Deligne in geometric normalisation, so that for ℓ ∤ Np the geometric Frobenius has characteristic polynomial X² − a_ℓ(f)X + ε(ℓ)ℓ^{k−1} and L(V_f, s) = L(f, s); and a G_Q-stable O-lattice T_f ⊂ V_f. Put T := T_f(det ρ_f^{-1}), V := T[1/p], A := V/T (so that T ≅ T_pE when f = f_E has weight two and trivial character), Γ := Gal(Q_∞/Q) for the cyclotomic Z_p-extension Q_∞, G_∞ := Gal(Q(μ_{p^∞})/Q) ≅ Δ × Γ with Δ ≅ (Z/p)^×, Λ := O[[Γ]], Λ(G_∞) := O[[G_∞]], γ ∈ Γ the generator corresponding to 1 + p under the cyclotomic character κ, and ι : Λ → Λ the involution induced by g ↦ g^{-1}. The residual representation ρ̄ is the reduction of T_f modulo ϖ; its semisimplification does not depend on T_f. The datum is ordinary when p ∤ N and a_p(f) ∈ O^×; then V_f has a unique G_{Q_p}-stable line V_f^+ on which inertia acts trivially, and T^+ := (T_f ∩ V_f^+)(det ρ_f^{-1}). The ordinary datum satisfies (dist) when the two characters of G_{Q_p} on ρ̄^{ss} restricted to G_{Q_p} are distinct, and (irred) when ρ̄ is irreducible.
hypotheses: p odd; f a newform; L contains the Hecke field and, for an ordinary datum, the roots of X² − a_p X + ε(p)p^{k−1}

geometric normalisation of ρ_f, as in Skinner–Urban; Kato's V_{F_λ}(f) is related to it by the dictionary of KatoEulerSystems:L2/hecke-dual-twist-dictionary, and Fouquet–Wan's cohomological ρ_f (det = χ_cyc^{1−k} for trivial ε) by ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L2/fw-convention-dictionary
proofSteps: Take ρ_f and its integral lattices from AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.5/ordinary-refinement-and-saturated-lattice (ordinary case) and R19.5/good-nonordinary-crystalline-wach-realisation (crystalline nonordinary case); the line V_f^+ and saturation T_f ∩ V_f^+ are the ordinary refinement supplied there (Skinner–Urban §1.1, p.2).

The twist by det ρ_f^{-1} is the one Skinner–Urban use to define their Selmer group (§1.1, p.2); for f = f_E the identification T ≅ T_pE comes from EllipticCurveModularity:R29.4/tate-module-comparison and the Weil pairing.
Λ, Λ(G_∞), the involution and the identification Λ ≅ O[[X]], γ ↦ 1 + X, are those of the completed group rings of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1.
acceptance: For f = f_E attached to 11a1 (weight 2, N = 11, ε = 1) and p = 7: a_7 = −2 ∈ Z_7^×, so the datum is ordinary; the unit root α of X² + 2X + 7 is congruent to −2 mod 7.
Changing T_f to ϖT_f gives the same T up to the isomorphism multiplication by ϖ; changing it to a non-homothetic lattice changes T but not ρ̄^{ss}.

nodes.title: The ordinary Selmer group over Q_∞ and its dual
nodes.statement: For an ordinary modular Iwasawa datum and a finite set Σ of primes not containing p, the Σ-imprimitive ordinary Selmer group is Sel^Σ(Q_∞, A) := the subgroup of H¹(Q_∞, A) of classes that are unramified at every finite place of Q_∞ not above p or Σ and whose restriction to the decomposition group at the unique place above p maps to zero in H¹(Q_{∞,p}, (T/T^+) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p); Sel(Q_∞, A) is the case Σ = ∅. Its Pontryagin dual X^Σ := Hom_cont(Sel^Σ(Q_∞, A), Q_p/Z_p) is a finitely generated Λ-module, with Λ acting on the dual through ι (the contragredient action). The same construction over Q(μ_{p^∞}) gives a Λ(G_∞)-module X^Σ(G_∞) whose η-components, for η ∈ Δ^∨, are the modules X^Σ of the twisted data f ⊗ η.
hypotheses: ordinary datum (p ∤ N, a_p ∈ O^×)
Σ finite, p ∉ Σ; the conditions at Σ are relaxed (no condition)
finite generation over Λ is unconditional; torsion is a theorem under hypotheses (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-selmer-structure), never part of the definition
proofSteps: Instantiate the Greenberg local condition SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/greenberg-condition at p with F^+ = T^+ and the unramified condition SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/unramified-condition away from pΣ, over the cyclotomic tower; the global group is SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/galois-selmer-group in its discrete form and the dual is SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/pontryagin-dual.

Skinner–Urban define the condition at p as vanishing in H¹(Q_{∞,p}, (T/T^+) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) (§1.1, p.2). Since Q_{∞,p}/Q_p is totally ramified, the kernel of H¹(Q_{∞,p}, A^-) → H¹(I, A^-) is A^-/(φ − 1)A^-, which is zero whenever the unramified Frobenius eigenvalue on A^- := (T/T^+) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p is not 1; so the strict and inertial forms agree unless α = 1, and the strict form is the one used.

Finite generation of X^Σ follows from that of H¹(Q_Σ'/Q_∞, A)^∨ over Λ (SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/iwasawa-finiteness-euler) by Nakayama over the compact local ring Λ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L5).

Relaxing Σ: X^Σ surjects onto X with kernel the dual of ⊕_{ℓ∈Σ} H¹(Q_{∞,ℓ}, A) (Skinner–Urban Proposition 3.2.18, p.27) when X is torsion and T* has no G_Q-fixed vectors.

nodes.title: Structure of the ordinary Selmer dual
nodes.statement: Let D be an ordinary modular Iwasawa datum with trivial character. (1) X^Σ is finitely generated over Λ. (2) If p ∤ N, then X is Λ-torsion (Kato 17.4(1)); for f = f_E with E/Q good ordinary or multiplicative at p, Z_∞ = Sel(E/Q_∞)^∨ is torsion. (3) If X^Σ is torsion, ρ̄ is irreducible, and Greenberg's local hypotheses hold (in the elliptic case: E good ordinary at p and p ∤ ∏_{q|N} #E(Q_q)_tors), then X^Σ has no nonzero finite Λ-submodule. (4) Under (3), char_Λ(X^Σ) = Fitt_Λ(X^Σ) is principal, and char_Λ(X^Σ) does not depend on the lattice T_f.
hypotheses: ordinary datum, trivial character
(2) uses p ∤ N for the non-elliptic case
(3) needs X^Σ torsion and the local hypotheses of Greenberg's theorem; for Σ-imprimitive X^Σ Skinner–Urban Lemma 3.2.17(i) gives the absence of pseudo-null submodules of the local terms
(4) the Fitting comparison is over Λ ≅ O[[X]] for modules with no nonzero finite submodule and projective dimension one
proofSteps: (1) is ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-selmer-dual's finiteness.

(2) is Kato Theorem 17.4(1) as planned in KatoEulerSystems:L4/ordinary-selmer-divisibility, and for elliptic curves KatoEulerSystems:L4/elliptic-ordinary-and-multiplicative-divisibility (Rubin III.5.14–5.16).
(3) is Greenberg's theorem in the form SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/selmer-no-pseudonull, and for elliptic curves Rubin Corollary 5.17 (KatoEulerSystems:L4/elliptic-no-finite-iwasawa-submodule).
(4) is SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/selmer-fitting-characteristic; lattice independence follows because irreducible ρ̄ forces homothetic lattices (Skinner–Urban §1.1, p.2).

Skinner's proof of Theorem A uses exactly (3)–(4): Ch^Σ(f_m) = F^Σ(f_m) for each member f_m of the Hida family (Skinner §1, p.3).

nodes.title: The ordinary p-adic L-function with canonical periods
nodes.statement: For an ordinary datum with trivial character and p ∤ N, let α be the unit root of X² − a_p X + p^{k−1} and Ω_f^± the canonical periods of f (generators of the saturated integral period lattices, defined up to O^× ∩ Q(f)). The ordinary p-adic L-function L_f ∈ Λ is the unique element such that for every finite-order character φ of Γ with φ(γ) = ζ a primitive p^{t−1}-th root of unity and every integer 0 ≤ m ≤ k − 2, φκ^m(L_f) = e(φκ^m)·p^{t'(m+1)} m! L(f, χ_φ^{-1}ω^{-m}, m+1) / ((−2πi)^m G(χ_φ^{-1}ω^{-m}) Ω_f^{sgn((−1)^m)}), with e the interpolation factor built from α, as in Skinner–Urban §1.1. For a finite set Σ of primes not containing p, L_f^Σ := L_f · ∏_{ℓ∈Σ} P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1}γ_ℓ), where P_{T,ℓ} is Skinner–Urban's Euler polynomial of T at ℓ (the polynomial of their Lemma 3.2.17(ii), so that the same factor appears on the Selmer side) and γ_ℓ ∈ Γ is the image of Frob_ℓ. L_f lies in Λ (not only Λ[1/p]) because the canonical periods are integral normalisations.
hypotheses: ordinary, p ∤ N, trivial character
canonical periods as supplied by ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/integral-period-lattices; a different choice changes L_f by an element of O^×
the measure is the ordinary branch of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/ordinary-integral-measure restricted to the cyclotomic Z_p-direction through the twist by ω^{-m}
proofSteps: Take the ordinary integral measure μ_{f,α} on Z_p^× of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/ordinary-integral-measure with the period lattice normalisation of ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/integral-period-lattices.

nodes.title: The Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture for an ordinary form
nodes.statement: For an ordinary datum D with trivial character and p ∤ N, and a finite set Σ of primes not containing p, IMC^Σ(D) is the proposition: X^Σ is a torsion Λ-module and char_Λ(X^Σ) = (L_f^Σ) as ideals of Λ. The rational form IMC^Σ_Q(D) asserts the same equality in Λ[1/p] = Λ ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p. For f = f_E it is Mazur's main conjecture in the normalisation of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/mazur-main-conjecture. The proposition is a statement, not an axiom: no theorem of this roadmap assumes it.
hypotheses: ordinary datum, trivial character, p ∤ N

the characteristic ideal is that of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 (charIdeal over the UFD Λ ≅ O[[X]])
proofSteps: Form X^Σ (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-selmer-dual) and L_f^Σ (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/canonical-ordinary-padic-l-function).
Use the characteristic ideal of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 §4.6; the rational form compares ideals after extension of scalars to Λ[1/p].

The integral statement is meaningful only after the period normalisation is fixed; Skinner–Urban §1.1 (p.2) note the characteristic ideal depends on T_f only through its ϖ-adic valuation, and not at all when ρ̄ is irreducible.
acceptance: IMC^Σ(D) for one Σ is equivalent to IMC^{Σ'}(D) for every Σ' (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5/euler-factor-change).
IMC(D) implies IMC_Q(D); the converse holds when μ(X) = μ(L_f) (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5/mu-lambda-comparison).

nodes.title: Iwasawa cohomology, the zeta element and the fundamental line
nodes.statement: For a modular Iwasawa datum with the lattice T_K in Kato's normalisation (the dictionary of KatoEulerSystems:L2/hecke-dual-twist-dictionary), put H^i(T_K) := lim_n H^i_et(Z[ζ_{p^n}, 1/p], j_*T_K) for i = 1, 2, Λ(G_∞)-modules, and RΓ_Iw(T_K) the corresponding perfect complex of Λ(G_∞)-modules with j_* conditions (extension by zero is not used; ramified primes keep the j_* condition). The Iwasawa fundamental line is the invertible Λ(G_∞)-module Δ_Iw(T_K) := Det^{-1}_{Λ(G_∞)} RΓ_Iw(T_K) ⊗ Det^{-1}_{Λ(G_∞)} (T_K ⊗ Λ(G_∞))(−1)^+, and Kato's zeta element z_f ∈ H¹(T_K) ⊗ Q (KatoEulerSystems:L2/integral-zeta-submodule-and-finite-index, the Λ-module Z(f, T_K) generated by Kato's zeta elements) defines, through the zeta morphism T_K(−1)^+ → H¹, a trivialisation triv_z : Δ_Iw(T_K) ⊗ Frac → Frac(Λ(G_∞)). The same construction over Q_∞ (Λ in place of Λ(G_∞)) gives Δ_Iw over Λ = O[[Γ]], the form used by Fouquet–Wan.

H¹(T_K) torsion-free of Λ-rank one and H²(T_K) torsion (Kato Theorem 12.4) are theorems, used to identify the determinant with an invertible fractional ideal
the {p}-partial complex over Z[1/p] is the one in Kato's Conjecture 12.10; the Σ-partial complex over Z[1/Σ] is used in families and changes Δ by Euler factors
proofSteps: Iwasawa cohomology and its finiteness are SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/iwasawa-cohomology and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/iwasawa-finiteness-euler; the étale/continuous comparison is SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/etale-iwasawa-comparison.
The determinant functor and the height-one divisor of an acyclic-after-Frac perfect complex are PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L5 §5.1 and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/selmer-determinant.

The zeta morphism is Kato's (KatoEulerSystems:L2/rational-kato-zeta-morphism and, over deformation rings, KatoEulerSystems:L2/nakamura-twisted-zeta-morphism); Fouquet–Wan Definition 3.3 and Theorem 3.4 record it as the {p}-partial zeta morphism z(f)_Iw.

nodes.title: Zeta basis versus characteristic ideals
nodes.statement: Let λ be an Iwasawa-suitable classical specialisation in the sense of Fouquet–Wan Definition 3.12 (in particular ρ̄ satisfies their Assumption 2.1 and there is ℓ ∥ N, ℓ ≠ p, with dim ρ̄^{I_ℓ} = 1). Then H¹(T_λ,Iw) is free of rank one over O_Iw, the cone of z(λ)_Iw : V_λ,Iw(−1)^+ → RΓ(Z[1/p], V_λ,Iw) is acyclic, its cohomology is H¹/z in degree one and H² in degree two, and consequently: z(λ)_Iw is a basis of Δ_Iw(T_λ) iff char H²(T_λ,Iw) = char(H¹(T_λ,Iw)/O_Iw·z(λ)_Iw). Moreover Kato's divisibility char(H¹/z) ⊂ char(H²) holds integrally for such λ.
hypotheses: Fouquet–Wan Assumption 2.1 (ρ̄|G_{Q(√p*)} absolutely irreducible; no extension 0 → χ₁ → ρ̄|G_{Q_p} → χ₂ → 0 with χ₁^{-1}χ₂ ∈ {1, χ̄_cyc}) and Assumption 3.7
λ Iwasawa-suitable: T_λ and T_λ*(1) relatively pure, z(ψ)_Iw nonzero for a contained O-valued specialisation
proofSteps: H¹ is torsion-free by vanishing of H⁰ of the reductions modulo regular sequences (Assumption 2.1), of depth two, hence free of rank one by Auslander–Buchsbaum–Serre (Fouquet–Wan Lemma 3.13).

Assumptions 2.1 and 3.7 give a unipotent element σ̄ ≠ 1 in the image of ρ̄, so T_λ/(σ − 1)T_λ is free of rank one; this verifies Kato's hypotheses in place of the SL₂(Z_p)-image condition (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/unipotent-rank-one-quotient), giving the integral divisibility and torsion of H².
With cohomology in degrees one and two only, the determinant of the cone is computed by ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/iwasawa-fundamental-line's divisor formula.
acceptance: For E = 14a1 at p = 13, ℓ = 2: ord_2 Δ = 6 is prime to 13, so ρ̄ is ramified at 2 with unipotent inertia image, dim ρ̄^{I_2} = 1, and the theorem applies.
The equivalence fails to make sense without freeness of H¹: if H¹ had torsion, Λ·z would not determine the line.

nodes.title: Kato's main conjecture versus the ordinary main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let D be an ordinary datum with trivial character, p ∤ N, p odd, with α the unit root, and let L_{p-adic,α,ω,γ}(f) be Kato's p-adic zeta function for a good pair (ω, γ) for the dual lattice. For every height-one prime 𝔭 of Λ not containing p there is an exact sequence of Λ_𝔭-modules 0 → (H¹/Z)_𝔭 → (H¹_loc/H¹_loc')_𝔭/(image of Z) → X_𝔭 → H²_𝔭 → 0 (Kato (17.13.1) localised), whose middle term has length ord_𝔭(L_{p-adic,α,ω,γ}(f)) by the Coleman map; hence length(X_𝔭) = ord_𝔭(L_{p-adic}) iff length(H²_𝔭) = length((H¹/Z)_𝔭). If in addition ρ̄ has a unipotent element with free rank-one coinvariants (or Kato's (12.5.2)) and p ≠ 2, the same holds at 𝔭 = (ϖ). Consequently KMC(T_K), on the η-component matched with D by Kato's twist T ↦ T(k) in (17.13.1), is equivalent to IMC(D), and KMC_Q to IMC_Q, once L_{p-adic,α,ω,γ}(f) is identified with L_f for the canonical periods (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/fw-ordinary-selmer-form for the integral identification).
hypotheses: ordinary at p, p ∤ N, p odd
(ω, γ) good for the dual lattice in Kato's sense (17.5), so Kato's p-adic L-function is integral
at the height-one prime (ϖ): Kato's (12.5.2) or the rank-one unipotent substitute of Skinner §2.5 and Fouquet–Wan Lemma 3.13
Euler and Tamagawa corrections: the sequence uses j_* conditions away from p and the Coleman image at p; no correction is discarded
proofSteps: Take the limit of the Poitou–Tate sequences for T(r) over Q(ζ_{p^n}) (SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/selmer-structure-poitou-tate, SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3/iwasawa-selmer-duality) to get Kato (17.13.1).

Show lim H¹_c of the strict condition vanishes (17.13.2) because the image of Z already has Λ-rank one, identify the local quotient with the Coleman map image (17.9; PadicHodgeRegulators:L3/rubin-coleman-map) and use finiteness of H²_loc (17.13.4).
Kato's explicit reciprocity (KatoEulerSystems:L3/generalised-explicit-reciprocity-law-for-zeta-elements) identifies the Coleman image of z with L_{p-adic,α,ω,γ}(f).
Compare lengths at each height-one prime; both directions of the equivalence follow from the additivity of length in the four-term sequence.
acceptance: Kato 17.13 derives Theorem 17.4(2)–(3) from Theorem 12.5 by this sequence, and remarks (p.274) that Conjecture 12.10 implies the ordinary main conjecture 17.6; the length identity gives the converse as well.
Fouquet–Wan Lemma 4.50 is the analogous equivalence with the signed or v^∨-Selmer group in place of X.

nodes.statement: Let D be a datum with p ∤ N whose local representation at p is crystalline, and fix a good basis ν₁, ν₂ of D_cris and its lift n₁, n₂ to the Wach module (LLZ §3.3, Lemma 3.15), giving Coleman maps Col_i : H¹_Iw(Q_p, T_K) → Λ_E(G_∞), i = 1, 2 (PadicHodgeRegulators:L4/signed-local-condition). For n ≥ 0 let H¹_f(Q_{p,n}, A^*)_i be the orthogonal complement, under the local Tate pairing between H¹(Q_{p,n}, T_K) and H¹(Q_{p,n}, A^*), of the image of ker(Col_i) in H¹(Q_{p,n}, T_K); here A^* is the discrete module paired with T_K in LLZ's Definition 6.4. nodes.title: The signed reformulation of Kato's main conjecture
nodes.statement: Assume LLZ's (A) if f is supersingular at p, or (A') if f is good ordinary, and (E): some basis of T_f has image of Gal(Q̄/Q_∞) containing SL₂(Z_p). Then for each η ∈ Δ^∨ (with i = 1 for every η and i = 2 for η trivial): X^{i,η} is Λ-torsion, there is an exact sequence 0 → (H¹/Z)^η → (Im(Col_i)/L̃_{p,i})^η → X^{i,η} → H²^η → 0, and KMC^η(T_K) ⟺ SMC^{i,η}. Without (E) the same holds rationally, and the divisibility ϖ^{n_i}L̃^η_{p,i} ∈ char(X^{i,η}) holds for some n_i ≥ 0.

(E) for the integral statement; the unipotent substitute of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/unipotent-rank-one-quotient supplies Kato's integral inputs but the equivalence as printed uses (E)
the η-restriction for i = 2 is LLZ's

Kato's divisibility Theorem 6.1(d)–(e) (KatoEulerSystems:L4/cohomological-divisibility-one-direction) gives the divisibility in Theorem 6.5.

(FW1.6_ℓ), in Fouquet–Wan's cohomological normalisation (det ρ̄ = χ̄_cyc^{1−k}): ℓ ≠ p, ℓ ∥ N, dim_F W^{I_ℓ} = 1 and dim_F W^{D_ℓ} = 0. (FWexp_ℓ(μ)): ℓ ≠ p and ρ̄|D_ℓ is a nonsplit extension 0 → μχ̄_cyc^{1−k/2} → ρ̄|D_ℓ → μχ̄_cyc^{−k/2} → 0 with μ unramified quadratic or trivial and ρ̄(I_ℓ) ≠ 1. (LocExc_p): there is no character χ̄ of D_p with (ρ̄|D_p)^{ss} ≅ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄χ̄_cyc. (ScalarExc_p): there is no χ̄ with (ρ̄|D_p)^{ss} ≅ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄. (Im): there is σ ∈ G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})} with T/(σ − 1)T free of rank one over O, for a lattice T lifting ρ̄. The predicates on W are lattice-independent except (Im), which is stated on T.

k is the weight of the form under consideration; (FWexp_ℓ) uses k even, automatic for trivial nebentypus

nodes.title: Skinner's theorem for multiplicative reduction
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) a newform with p ∥ N (so f is ordinary at p, k = 2, and a_p = ±1), L/Q_p as in the datum, (irred) for ρ̄_f, and a prime q ≠ p with q ∥ N and ρ̄_f ramified at q. Hida theory: f is the weight-two member of a Hida family (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.6/ordinary-newform-lies-in-a-hida-family); for each m > 0 there is a newform f_m ∈ S_{k_m}(Γ_0(N/p)) with k_m ≡ 2 mod (p − 1)p^m, ordinary, whose p-stabilisation is congruent to f modulo p^m.
Two-variable p-adic L-function: L^Σ_{f_m} ≡ L^Σ_f mod p^m Λ, from the family p-adic L-function of the branch (PadicFamilies:L1/branch-l-functions).

Greenberg's theorem (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-selmer-structure) gives Ch^Σ(f_m) = Fitt(X^Σ(f_m)); the congruence gives Sel^Σ(f)[p^m] ≅ Sel^Σ(f_m)[p^m], hence (Fitt(X^Σ(f)), p^m) = (Ch^Σ(f_m), p^m) = (L^Σ_{f_m}, p^m) = (L^Σ_f, p^m) for every m.
Since L^Σ_f ≠ 0, Fitt(X^Σ(f)) ≠ 0, so X^Σ(f) is torsion, Greenberg's theorem gives Ch^Σ(f) = Fitt, and principal ideals agreeing modulo every p^m are equal.

nodes.title: The Fouquet–Wan pointwise main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3, F a finite field of characteristic p and ρ̄ : G_Q → GL₂(F) absolutely irreducible and odd, satisfying: (LocExc_p) and (ScalarExc_p); and for some ℓ ≠ p, (FWexp_ℓ(μ)) — a ramified extension 0 → μχ̄_cyc^{1−k/2} → ρ̄|D_ℓ → μχ̄_cyc^{−k/2} → 0 with μ unramified, and μ nontrivial if ρ̄|G_{Q_p} is irreducible. Then KMC^{η=1} holds for f integrally: the zeta morphism induces Δ_{O_Iw}(T(f)_Iw) ≅ O_Iw (Fouquet–Wan Conjecture 3.24 = 1.5). nodes.statement: Let E/Q, p > 3 a prime of good ordinary reduction with E[p] irreducible. Then X_ord(E/Q_∞) is Λ-torsion and MMC_Q(E, p) holds: char_{Λ_Q}(X_ord(E/Q_∞)) = (L_p(E/Q)) in Λ ⊗ Q_p. No ramification hypothesis on E[p] is assumed.
hypotheses: p > 3, good ordinary, (irr_Q)
the proof owner is AutomorphicCongruences:L5b; this node transports its endpoint into the formulation of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/mazur-main-conjecture
proofSteps: Import AutomorphicCongruences:L5b/rational-cyclotomic-endpoint (base change to the quartic CM field, Wan's divisibility, the four-factor descent and Kato's bounds).

Translate its Selmer and analytic objects with ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/curve-form-lattice-dictionary and ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/msd-padic-l-function; the rational form needs no Manin-constant input.
acceptance: Applies to 11a1 at p = 7 and to 14a1 at p = 13; it does not apply at p = 3 or at Eisenstein primes (11a1 at p = 5).

It removes the ramification hypothesis (mult) of Skinner–Urban: 11a1 at p = 7 is covered by both, while a curve with no multiplicative prime at which E[p] ramifies (e.g. a curve of prime conductor ℓ with p | ord_ℓ Δ) is covered only here.

nodes.title: The Burungale–Castella–Skinner integral cyclotomic theorem

proofSteps: Import AutomorphicCongruences:L5b/integral-cyclotomic-endpoint and transport it as in the rational case.

The integral form needs L_p(E/Q) ∈ Λ (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/msd-padic-l-function under (irr_Q)) and the Manin-constant comparison (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/curve-form-lattice-dictionary).

nodes.title: Residual surjectivity gives the rank-one image condition
nodes.statement: Let E/Q, p ≥ 5, and suppose ρ̄_{E,p} : G_Q → GL₂(F_p) is surjective. Then the image of ρ_{E,p^∞} is GL₂(Z_p), the image of G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})} contains SL₂(Z_p), and σ with ρ_{E,p^∞}(σ) = [[1, 1], [0, 1]] satisfies T_pE/(σ − 1)T_pE ≅ Z_p, so (Im) holds.
hypotheses: residual surjectivity onto GL₂(F_p)
proofSteps: A closed subgroup of SL₂(Z_p) surjecting onto SL₂(F_p) is SL₂(Z_p) for p ≥ 5 (Serre's lemma), so the image is GL₂(Z_p) (the determinant is the cyclotomic character, surjective onto Z_p^×).
Q(μ_{p^∞}) is cut out by the determinant, so G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})} maps onto SL₂(Z_p) ∩ image = SL₂(Z_p).
For u = [[1,1],[0,1]], u − 1 has image Z_p·e₁, so the quotient is free of rank one (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1/unipotent-rank-one-quotient).
acceptance: For E = 14a1 and p = 5 (5 is not a nonmaximal prime for 14a1), ρ̄_{E,5} is surjective, so (Im) holds.
Burungale–Castella–Skinner Remark 1.1.3(i): for non-CM E, (Im) holds for all sufficiently large p by Serre's open image theorem.

sources.match: (im) for large p by Serre's open image theorem; residual surjectivity (sur) as the integral hypothesis in the anticyclotomic theorem

nodes.title: The Fouquet–Wan universal-family main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ satisfy the hypotheses of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L2/fw-pointwise-theorem, Σ a finite set of primes, and T_Σ the universal deformation of ρ̄ unramified outside Σ, viewed as a free module of finite rank over the regular subring Λ ≅ O[[X₁, X₂, X₃]] of the Hecke algebra. Let z_Σ : T_Σ(−1)^+ → H¹_et(Z[1/Σ], T_Σ) be Nakamura's zeta morphism. Then z_Σ induces an isomorphism triv_{z_Σ} : Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ≅ Λ of the Σ-partial fundamental line with Λ: Kato's generalised main conjecture (Fouquet–Wan Conjecture 3.30) holds for (Spec Z[1/Σ], Λ, T_Σ). The trivialisation is over Λ; nothing is asserted over a possibly singular deformation ring or Hecke algebra.
hypotheses: the residual hypotheses of the pointwise theorem (Fouquet–Wan Theorem 5.2: the same as Theorem 5.1)
Λ ≅ O[[X₁,X₂,X₃]] is the specified regular subring; T_Σ is free of finite rank over it
Nakamura's zeta morphism exists under Fouquet–Wan Assumptions 2.1 and 3.5 (Theorem 3.6), for all p ≥ 3 by the remark after it

The zeta morphism is KatoEulerSystems:L2/nakamura-twisted-zeta-morphism; the Σ-partial line is ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/iwasawa-fundamental-line over Λ.
This node exposes the endpoint with its exact coefficient ring and no strengthening.

When the deformation problem is unobstructed, R_Σ(ρ̄) is itself a power-series ring and the theorem is the most general cyclotomic statement (Fouquet–Wan p.8).

nodes.title: Specialising the family statement
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L4/fw-universal-family-theorem, let ψ : Λ → S be an Iwasawa-suitable specialisation (Fouquet–Wan Definition 3.12), with associated Λ_Iw-adic specialisation ψ_Iw. Then the canonical isomorphism Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ⊗^L S_Iw ≅ Δ_Σ(T_ψ,Iw) carries triv_{z_Σ} to triv_{z_Σ(ψ_Iw)}, so Kato's Σ-partial conjecture (Fouquet–Wan Conjecture 3.25) holds at ψ. At a classical point λ_f, passing from the Σ-partial to the {p}-partial line multiplies the trivialisation by ∏_{ℓ∈Σ∖{p}} Eul_ℓ(T(f)_Iw), each factor nonzero (relative purity), so KMC^{η=1}(f) follows. The specialisation is a derived base change: when RΓ(Z[1/Σ], T_ψ) is not concentrated in degrees one and two, or the module structure of H² does not specialise, the characteristic-ideal form at ψ is deduced only through the determinant, never by specialising characteristic ideals termwise; Tor terms are kept.
hypotheses: ψ Iwasawa-suitable (Fouquet–Wan Definition 3.12)
Euler factors Eul_ℓ as in Fouquet–Wan Definition 3.8, nonvanishing by Lemma 3.11 and Proposition 3.10
proofSteps: Fouquet–Wan Proposition 3.23: RΓ_et(Z[1/Σ], −) commutes with change of coefficients and preserves perfect complexes, so the trivialisations correspond (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L5 for determinants of perfect complexes and specialisation).
Compare Σ- and {p}-partial lines by the local Euler factors (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/iwasawa-fundamental-line, fundamentalLine.sigmaPartial).
Translate to KMC through ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/zeta-basis-characteristic-equivalence at Iwasawa-suitable points.
acceptance: At a point where H⁰ or a Tor term is nonzero, termwise specialisation of char(H²) would be wrong; the determinant form remains valid.

The family statement implies the pointwise conjecture outside a closed subset of positive codimension (Fouquet–Wan p.8); the pointwise theorem at every classical point is ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L2/fw-pointwise-theorem.

nodes.title: The signed main conjecture for crystalline forms

nodes.title: Removing the Coleman-image term

Then Col₁ : N(V)^{ψ=1} → Λ_E(G_∞) is surjective (LLZ Theorem 4.28), so Im(Col₁) = Λ_E(G_∞) and, after tensoring with Q, KMC^η is equivalent to char(X^{1,η}) = (L̃^η_{p,1}) (LLZ Corollary 6.8). nodes.title: Kobayashi's and Pollack's signed objects
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have good supersingular reduction at an odd prime p with a_p = 0. For the LLZ basis there are units a^± ∈ Λ_E(G_∞)^× with a^−·Col₁ = Col^− and a^+·Col₂ = Col^+, where Col^± are the plus and minus Coleman maps whose kernels define Kobayashi's local conditions E^±; consequently (1) the signed Selmer groups X¹, X² of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/signed-selmer-dual are Kobayashi's Sel^−(E/Q_∞)^∨ and Sel^+(E/Q_∞)^∨; (2) L̃_{p,1}, L̃_{p,2} are Pollack's L_p^−, L_p^+ up to units of Λ_E(G_∞), and the decomposition of L̃_{p,α}, L̃_{p,β} in LLZ Theorem 1.3 reduces to Pollack's decomposition with the half-logarithms log^±_p; (3) SMC^{1,η}, SMC^{2,η} are Kobayashi's minus and plus main conjectures char(Sel^∓(E/Q_∞)^{∨,η}) = char(Im(Col^∓)^η/(L_p^{∓,η})). The comparison is specific to a_p = 0; for a_p ≠ 0 the LLZ objects are not Pollack's plus/minus objects without a separate argument.

nodes.title: Changing the imprimitive set: Euler factors on both sides
nodes.statement: Let D be an ordinary datum with trivial character, p ∤ N, and Σ' ⊂ Σ finite sets of primes not containing p. If X^Σ is Λ-torsion and T* has no nonzero G_Q-invariants, then 0 → (⊕_{ℓ∈Σ∖Σ'} H¹(Q_{∞,ℓ}, A))^∨ → X^Σ → X^{Σ'} → 0 is exact, each local term is torsion with no nonzero pseudo-null submodule and characteristic ideal (P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1}γ_ℓ)), where P_{T,ℓ} is the Euler polynomial of Skinner–Urban Lemma 3.2.17(ii) and γ_ℓ ∈ Γ is the image of Frob_ℓ; hence char(X^Σ) = char(X^{Σ'})·∏_{ℓ∈Σ∖Σ'} (P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1}γ_ℓ)). On the analytic side L_f^Σ = L_f^{Σ'}·∏_{ℓ∈Σ∖Σ'} P_{T,ℓ}(ℓ^{-1}γ_ℓ) with the same factors. Therefore IMC^Σ(D) ⟺ IMC^{Σ'}(D), integrally and rationally, and the same holds for KMC with Σ-partial lines.
hypotheses: X^Σ torsion (it then follows for Σ')
T* has no nonzero G_Q-invariants (true when ρ̄ is irreducible)

Analytic side: ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L4/primitive-imprimitive-level-change.

Since Λ → Λ_{O'} is faithfully flat, IMC^Σ(D ⊗ O') ⟺ IMC^Σ(D), and similarly for KMC and SMC.

nodes.title: μ- and λ-invariants of the two sides
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser ϖ, Λ = O[[X]], and f, g ∈ Λ nonzero. If (f)Λ[1/ϖ] = (g)Λ[1/ϖ] and ϖ^n | f ⟺ ϖ^n | g for all n (equal μ-invariants), then f and g are associated in Λ. Consequently: (1) IMC(D) implies μ(X) = μ(L_f) and λ(X) = λ(L_f); (2) IMC_Q(D) together with μ(X) = μ(L_f) implies IMC(D); (3) the same holds for KMC and Mazur's conjecture; in particular IMC_Q(D) and μ(L_f) = 0 = μ(X) give the integral conjecture.

For (1): Weierstrass preparation f = ϖ^μ P u (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 §4.3–4.4) and char(X) = (ϖ^{μ(X)} char-poly) give equality of invariants.

nodes.title: The rank-zero p-converse
nodes.statement: (1) (Skinner–Urban) Let E/Q, p a prime of good ordinary reduction with ρ̄_{E,p} irreducible and a prime q ≠ p, q ∥ N_E, at which ρ̄_{E,p} is ramified. If Sel_{p^∞}(E/Q) is finite then L(E,1) ≠ 0; equivalently, L(E,1) = 0 implies corank_{Z_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/Q) ≥ 1. The same holds at p of multiplicative reduction under Skinner's Theorem C hypotheses. (3) For f = f_E with E/Q and N not squarefull (Skinner–Urban) or arbitrary N (Wan), if rank E(Q) = 0 and Sha(E/Q)[p^∞] is finite for one sufficiently large ordinary p, then ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = 0.

nodes.title: The Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum p-adic BSD conjecture
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have good ordinary or multiplicative reduction at an odd p, r = rank E(Q), α the unit root, L_{p,α}(E, s) the function of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/msd-padic-l-function, ⟨ , ⟩_{p,α} the p-adic height on Q_p ⊗ E(Q) attached to the splitting of the Hodge filtration given by the α-eigenline of Frobenius, and R_{p,α}(E) its regulator. MTT(E, p) is the proposition: (i) if α ≠ 1, ord_{s=1} L_{p,α}(E, s) ≥ r and lim_{s→1} (s − 1)^{−r} L_{p,α}(E, s) = (1 − α^{-1})^{b+1}·#Sha(E)·R_{p,α}(E)·∏_v m_v; (ii) if α = 1, the order is ≥ r + 1 and lim_{s→1} (s − 1)^{−r−1} L_{p,α}(E, s) = ℒ_p(E)·#Sha(E)·R_{p,α}(E)·∏_v m_v. Here, as in Colmez Conjecture 0.12, R_{p,α}(E) := e^{−2} det(⟨P_i, P_j⟩_{p,α}) for P_1, …, P_r spanning Q ⊗ E(Q) and generating a subgroup of index e in E(Q) (so R_{p,α}(E) = #E(Q)_tors^{−2} when r = 0), m_v is the number of components at v (m_∞ for E(R), the Tamagawa number at finite v), and Ω_E^+ satisfies m_∞Ω_E^+ = |∫_{E(R)} ω_E|.
hypotheses: good ordinary or multiplicative p, p odd
the p-adic height pairing is an input (the Mazur–Tate/Schneider height for ordinary E); its nondegeneracy is not known in general
the torsion enters through the index e in the regulator, as in Colmez's normalisation of R_∞(E); the formula must not divide by #E(Q)_tors² a second time
proofSteps: State with L_{p,α}(E, s) (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3/msd-padic-l-function), ℒ_p(E) (ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5/tate-l-invariant) and the p-adic height.

The p-adic height pairing and regulator are an input with no planned owner in the atlas (gap: the SelmerIwasawaCohomology Part II on p-adic heights is not yet a roadmap; NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.7/height-pairing-bockstein plans Nekovář's height only as a Bockstein map).
acceptance: Kato's theorem (Colmez Theorem 0.15): ord_{s=1} L_{p,α}(E,s) ≥ r (≥ r + 1 if α = 1), and equality implies Sha[p^∞] finite and R_{p,α}(E) ≠ 0 — a consequence, not an assumption.
In rank zero with α ≠ 1, MTT(E, p) is equivalent to the p-part of the classical BSD formula (the factor (1 − α^{-1})² is a p-adic unit times what BSD predicts).

nodes.title: Trivial zeros in analytic rank zero
nodes.statement: Let E/Q have good ordinary or multiplicative reduction at an odd prime p with L(E,1) ≠ 0. Then ord_{s=1} L_{p,α}(E, s) ∈ {0, 1}, with order one iff E has split multiplicative reduction at p (α = 1), and in that case L'_{p,α}(E, 1) = ℒ_p(E)·L(E,1)/Ω_E^+ (Greenberg–Stevens) with ℒ_p(E) ≠ 0. gaps.title: No owner for the p-adic height pairing of an elliptic curve
gaps.detail: The Mazur–Tate/Schneider p-adic height ⟨ , ⟩_{p,α} on E(Q) and its regulator R_{p,α}(E) are needed to state MTT and Schneider's implication. The atlas has only Nekovář's height as a Bockstein map (NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.7/height-pairing-bockstein); the 'SelmerIwasawaCohomology, Part II: p-adic height pairings' direction accepted in the review of PAPER-DISEGNI-LIU-24 is not yet a roadmap (its design job is open). Until it exists the two nodes cite NE.7 and this gap.

gaps.title: Schneider's leading-term theorem not read
gaps.detail: Schneider, 'p-adic height pairings II', Invent. Math. 79 (1985) was not available freely; the plan cites it through Rodrigues Jacinto–Williams Remark 2.3 and Colmez's note 14. The exact statement (order of vanishing of the characteristic power series at the trivial character and its leading coefficient, with Tamagawa and torsion factors) must be taken from it or a later complete account before the node is refined.

gaps.title: Scalar exclusion at p in Fouquet–Wan's pointwise theorem
gaps.detail: Fouquet–Wan's standing Assumption 2.1(2) excludes (ρ̄|G_{Q_p})^{ss} ≅ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄ and Theorem 1.1 lists that exclusion, but Theorems 1.7 and 5.1 do not. The plan keeps the exclusion as a hypothesis; removing it needs an argument from the owner AutomorphicCongruences:L4 (source issue ModularIwasawaMainConjectures/E1).

gaps.title: Ramification at 5 in the higher-weight example
gaps.detail: For f = η(z)⁴η(5z)⁴ at p = 7, ramification of ρ̄ at 5 follows from Mazur's principle in weight 4 ≤ p + 1 (5 ≢ 1 mod 7, S_4(SL₂(Z)) = 0); the cited level-lowering statement in weight 4 has not been fixed. The example is not used by any theorem.

gaps.title: Iwasawa main conjectures for imaginary quadratic fields (RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/5)
gaps.detail: The Eisenstein-prime branch interface re-exports RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.7a's integral cyclotomic theorems, which rest on Rubin's two-variable main conjecture via elliptic units, the Hida–Tilouine anticyclotomic main conjecture and Hida's μ = 0 for anticyclotomic Katz p-adic L-functions, none of which any roadmap plans. The restructure entry proposes the owning roadmap; this interface carries the gap until it exists.

gaps.title: Canonical versus Gross periods
gaps.detail: Deducing Fouquet–Wan Theorem 1.6 from Skinner–Urban's U(2,2) argument would need a comparison of canonical and Gross periods that, as Fouquet–Wan note (p.6), is not in the literature in the required generality. The plan does not use it: L1/fw-ordinary-theorem follows the §4.8 route owned by AutomorphicCongruences:L2, and L1/su-ordinary-theorem keeps Skinner–Urban's own hypotheses. Any alternative route through the comparison must first supply it.

requests.need: Skinner–Urban's GU(2,2) reverse divisibility in its source range: for p ≥ 3, f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(N)) ordinary with trivial character, k ≡ 2 mod p − 1, (irred), (dist), p ∤ N, and an imaginary quadratic K with p split, the prime divisors of N/q split and q inert for a prime q ∥ N at which ρ̄ ramifies: Ch^Σ(f)·Ch^Σ(f ⊗ χ_K) ⊂ (L_f^Σ L_{f⊗χ_K}^Σ) for Σ ⊇ {ℓ | pND_K} (Skinner–Urban Theorem 3.6.1 and Corollary 3.6.3, pp.41–42), with the integral form requiring only (irred) and the rank-one unipotent element (Skinner 2016 §2.5). Export it in the normalisation of ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0/ordinary-selmer-dual and L0/canonical-ordinary-padic-l-function.

Fouquet–Wan §4.8's reverse divisibility for Theorem 1.6: for p > 2, f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(N)), p ∤ N, k ≥ 2, ρ̄_f absolutely irreducible, some ℓ ∥ N with dim ρ̄^{I_ℓ} = 1 and dim ρ̄^{G_ℓ} = 0 (cohomological normalisation), and the ordinary filtration with χ̄₁ ≠ χ̄₂: char(H¹(Z[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw)/Λ_Iw·z(f)_Iw) | char(H²(Z[1/p], T ⊗ Λ_Iw)), proved through the GU(3,1) divisibility (Fouquet–Wan Theorem 7.32), Beilinson–Flach explicit reciprocity and Poitou–Tate as in Castella–Wan Theorem 3.8 extended to weight k, with the Kato twist/factor separation. This is RS-11's owner record; no canonical/Gross period comparison is to be assumed.

Fouquet–Wan's pointwise and universal-family endpoints exactly as in Theorems 5.1–5.2 (and 1.7–1.8): (pointwise) for p ≥ 3, ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and odd with (ρ̄|G_{Q_p})^{ss} ≠ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄χ̄_cyc, ℓ ≠ p with ρ̄|D_ℓ a ramified extension 0 → μχ̄_cyc^{1−k/2} → ρ̄ → μχ̄_cyc^{−k/2} → 0 (μ unramified, nontrivial if ρ̄|G_{Q_p} is irreducible), and f ∈ S_k(Γ_0(Np^r)) with ρ̄_f ≅ ρ̄, ℓ ∥ N: the zeta morphism gives Δ_{O_Iw}(T(f)_Iw) ≅ O_Iw; (family) triv_{z_Σ} : Δ_Σ(T_Σ) ≅ Λ over the regular subring Λ ≅ O[[X₁,X₂,X₃]]. State whether the scalar exclusion (ρ̄|G_{Q_p})^{ss} ≠ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄ of Fouquet–Wan Assumption 2.1(2) is needed (source issue ModularIwasawaMainConjectures/E1).

The completed group rings O[[Γ]], O[[G_∞]] with the involution g ↦ g^{-1}, the identification O[[Γ]] ≅ O[[X]] by γ ↦ 1 + X, and Λ(G_∞) ≅ O[Δ][[Γ]] (TauCetiRoadmap PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras layer 1).

charIdeal and charDivisor over Λ = O[[X]] with multiplicativity in exact sequences, pseudo-isomorphism invariance, base change along O → O', the isotypic decomposition over Λ(Δ × Γ), μ- and λ-invariants and Weierstrass preparation (TauCetiRoadmap PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §§4.3–4.6).

Determinant lines of perfect complexes over Λ and their compatibility with base change and specialisation, and topological Nakayama for compact Λ-modules (TauCetiRoadmap PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §§5.1–5.2).

Greenberg–Stevens (Invent. Math. 111 (1993), Theorem 7.1): for E/Q with split multiplicative reduction at p, L'_{p,α}(E,1) = ℒ_p(E)·L(E,1)/Ω_E^+ (Colmez Theorem 0.11), via the Mazur–Kitagawa two-variable p-adic L-function; the same request is made by RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0 (RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/4(b)).

Barré-Sirieix–Diaz–Gramain–Philibert (1996): for E/Q with split multiplicative reduction at p, the Tate parameter q_E is transcendental, hence log_p(q_E) ≠ 0 and ℒ_p(E) ≠ 0 (Colmez Remark 0.13(i)); the same request is made by RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0 (RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/4(c)).

The Tate curve over Q_p for split multiplicative E: the Tate parameter q_E with |q_E| < 1, the isomorphism E(Q̄_p) ≅ Q̄_p^×/q_E^Z, ord_p(q_E) = ord_p(Δ_min), and its p-th-power criterion for ramification of E[p] at ℓ (E[p] unramified at ℓ iff p | ord_ℓ(q_E)).

The Coates–Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin existence proposition for an ordinary V attached to a motive (realisation, critical set, Deligne periods, refinement and interpolation factors), in the form against which L_f of a weight-k ordinary newform can be checked (RS-11: I.L5 imports it).

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv:2107.13726v3, Theorem 1.7 (p.7) and Theorem 5.1 (p.68), against Theorem 1.1 (p.3) and Assumption 2.1(2) (p.17)
sourceIssues.printed: Theorems 1.7 and 5.1 list as local hypothesis at p only that the semisimplification of ρ̄|G_{Q_p} is not of the form χ̄ ⊕ χ̄χ̄_cyc; Theorem 1.1 also excludes χ̄ ⊕ χ̄, and the standing Assumption 2.1(2) of §2 excludes extensions with χ₁^{-1}χ₂ = 1.
sourceIssues.correction: State Theorems 1.7 and 5.1 with the additional exclusion (ρ̄|G_{Q_p})^{ss} ≠ χ̄ ⊕ χ̄, or supply an argument for the scalar case.
sourceIssues.reason: The proofs run through §2–§4, which assume Assumption 2.1 throughout (representability and scalar endomorphisms of ρ̄|G_{Q_p}, Lemma 3.13's vanishing of H⁰); the theorems' hypotheses (2)–(3) imply Assumption 2.1(1) and Assumption 3.5 but not the scalar part of 2.1(2).
searched: arXiv versions v1–v3 abstract pages and the v3 text, read 18 October 2026; no erratum found by a bounded web search the same day; no claim of exhaustive novelty.

sourceIssues.printed: Assumption 3 (ℓ ∥ N, dim ρ̄^{I_ℓ} = 1, dim ρ̄^{G_{Q_ℓ}} = 0) is said to be equivalent to π(f)_ℓ being Steinberg twisted by the unramified character sending ℓ to −ℓ^{k/2−1}, with ρ̄|G_ℓ ramified.
sourceIssues.correction: The equivalence holds in weight two. In general, with ρ̄|D_ℓ a ramified extension of μχ̄_cyc^{−k/2} by μχ̄_cyc^{1−k/2}, the condition dim ρ̄^{D_ℓ} = 0 means μ(ℓ)ℓ^{1−k/2} ≢ 1 mod ϖ, which neither implies nor is implied by μ(ℓ) = −1 when k > 2.
sourceIssues.reason: The inertia-invariant line is the sub-line μχ̄_cyc^{1−k/2} (cohomological normalisation, as in Theorem 1.7), whose arithmetic Frobenius eigenvalue is μ(ℓ)ℓ^{1−k/2}; for k = 4 and ℓ ≡ −1 mod p with μ(ℓ) = −1 the eigenvalue is 1, and with μ(ℓ) = 1, ℓ ≢ 1 mod p it is not.
searched: arXiv v3 text read 18 October 2026; the theorems themselves are stated with their own hypotheses, so only the remark is affected; bounded web search found no correction.
